title: Casper and the Verdict
premise: When a confession letter arrives at coroner Noor Kavanagh's office postmarked the day after Edith Verrell's funeral, it names three 'accidents' Noor already suspected were murders — and promises a fourth before the anniversary dinner. Following the letter's clues, Noor discovers the town's founding family kept a ledger disguised as a hymnal in the church archive, recording debts, bribes, and payments for silence spanning sixty years. The trail leads to her own late mentor, whose loyalty to the Verrells cost him his conscience and nearly hers. At the anniversary dinner, Noor exposes the surviving heir who has been killing to keep the inheritance clean, choosing truth over the protective silence that once defined this town.
about_author: R. M. Eriksen is the pen name of a former rural journalist who spent a decade covering small-town courtrooms and county funerals. They write mysteries about the quiet bargains people make with their own communities.

chapters.title: The Day After
chapters.summary: Noor Kavanagh, POV. Two days after Edith Verrell's funeral, a confession letter arrives postmarked the day after the burial — impossible timing. It names three deaths Noor ruled suspicious but couldn't prove. Emotional beat: dread mixed with vindication; someone out there knows what she knows.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She walks the cemetery, revisiting the three 'accidents': a drowned fisherman, a fallen roofer, a burned-out car. Flashbacks establish her quiet history of being overruled by police. Beat: loneliness of the truth-keeper; she decides to answer the letter.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Invitation
chapters.summary: Deputy Sam Okafor's POV. The Verrell estate announces its sixtieth anniversary dinner, and all three accident victims' families are invited — an odd gesture of charity. Sam notices Noor pulling case files. Beat: institutional suspicion; the clock starts ticking toward the dinner.

chapters.title: Reply Not Required
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A second letter arrives: instructions hidden in a newspaper crossword, pointing to the church archive. The writer warns that the fourth death is already scheduled. Beat: complicity — by following the clues, Noor becomes part of the confession.

chapters.title: Hymnal 212
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. In the church archive she finds a hymnal whose numbered pages map to a ledger of the Verrell family's debts, bribes, and hush payments across sixty years. Three names are marked with a black cross. Beat: awe curdling into fear as the pattern becomes undeniable.

chapters.title: What the Fisherman Owed
chapters.summary: Marta Reyes, widow of the drowned man, POV. Marta recalls her husband's fear in his final weeks and a payment he received from the Verrell account. She lies to Sam Okafor to protect her children. Beat: the price of survival — silence bought and paid for.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The ledger's earliest entries are in the handwriting of Dr. Aldous Pike, Noor's late mentor, who taught her forensic medicine. He signed off on all three 'accidents.' Beat: betrayal; the ground beneath her career gives way.

chapters.title: Sixty Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Alternating Noor and archival documents. The ledger reveals the original sin: a 1965 fire at the Verrell mill that killed four workers, covered up to protect the inheritance of the then-heir. Beat: inheritance as curse; every death since has been maintenance of a lie.

chapters.title: Sam Asks Questions
chapters.summary: Sam Okafor's POV. Sam confronts Noor about the missing files and follows her to the church. Torn between duty and trust, he copies one ledger page before she catches him. Beat: loyalty vs. truth begins to fracture their alliance.

chapters.title: The Roofer's Daughter
chapters.summary: Tessa Brandt, daughter of the fallen roofer, POV. Tessa received anonymous money for years after her father's death and assumed it was guilt. Now someone has asked her to attend the dinner and say nothing. Beat: the survivors' bargain exposed; she agrees to help Noor.

chapters.title: Postmark Problems
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor proves the letters were written years ago and held for mailing — meaning the confessor planned this long ago or is dead and scripted. The handwriting analysis points somewhere impossible. Beat: the mystery deepens; the confessor may be one of the dead.

chapters.title: Dinner Preparations
chapters.summary: Cyrus Verrell, current patriarch, POV. Cyrus rehearses his toast and instructs staff on seating, revealing he knows more about the family history than he admits. His son Adrian watches him with cold patience. Beat: menace inside respectability; the heir apparent circles.

chapters.title: A Fourth Name
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Decoding further ledger entries, Noor finds a fourth name marked in fresh ink: her own. The letters weren't a confession — they were a warning meant to save her. Beat: terror and gratitude entwined; she understands the stakes.

chapters.title: Pike's Last Patient
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Aldous Pike's POV (via journal). Weeks before his death, Pike discovered the ledger, confronted the family, and chose loyalty over truth — agreeing to stay silent in exchange for Noor's safety. Beat: tragic compromise; the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Unknown assailant's POV (unnamed). Someone burns the church archive annex overnight. Noor, tipped by the organist, rescues the hymnal minutes ahead of the flames. Beat: escalation; the killer knows how close she is.

chapters.title: Alliances and Alibis
chapters.summary: Sam's POV. Sam covers for Noor with the sheriff while privately building his own case file. He and Noor strike an uneasy pact: truth first, law second. Beat: repaired loyalty on new terms; the alliance reforged.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor decodes the final ledger page: the anniversary toast itself is the signal, and the fourth death is set for midnight at the Verrell house. She identifies the likely target — Cyrus. Beat: breathless urgency; everything converges on tomorrow night.

chapters.title: Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs intercut. The dinner unfolds in opulent tension: the toast is raised, Tessa and Marta sit among the heirs, and Noor attends uninvited under Sam's escort. Adrian delivers the toast with a poisoned glass set beside his father's. Beat: peak suspense; the trap springs.

chapters.title: The Glass Raised
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. At the toast, Noor swaps the glasses and forces the confrontation, reading the ledger aloud. Adrian's composure cracks when the postmark evidence ties him to the letters' mailing schedule. Beat: climax; truth spoken aloud in the lion's den.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Ash
chapters.summary: Adrian's POV. Cornered, Adrian confesses the logic of his killings: protecting the inheritance from the mill fire's truth, just as his grandfather did. Sam arrests him as Cyrus collapses — not poisoned, but broken by exposure. Beat: the murderer's creed dismantled.

chapters.title: What We Bury
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Aftermath: the mill fire victims are publicly named, the ledger enters evidence, and Pike's grave gets a visitor who leaves both forgiveness and a copy of the truth. Beat: grief and release; loyalty redefined as honesty.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name, Again
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, one year later. Noor walks the cemetery adding four new headstones to her mental map, including Adrian's. A new letter arrives — different handwriting, different town. Beat: quiet resolve; the price of survival was worth paying, and the work continues.
